perplexity.description:
Released in 1993 by Warner Bros. Records, Coneheads (Music From The Motion Picture Soundtrack) is a diverse compilation that blends rock, pop, and classic tracks, reflecting the quirky, comedic tone of the film. The album features a mix of original songs and covers, including standout performances such as Red Hot Chili Peppers’ “Soul to Squeeze,” which became a major hit and reached number one on the Modern Rock chart, and k.d. lang and Andy Bell’s energetic rendition of “No More Tears (Enough Is Enough).” Other notable inclusions are Slash and Michael Monroe’s take on “Magic Carpet Ride,” Barenaked Ladies’ cover of “Fight the Power,” and Paul Simon’s “Kodachrome,” all contributing to the soundtrack’s eclectic and playful character.

As a Various Artists release, the album does not fit within a single artist’s discography but serves as a snapshot of early 1990s pop culture and alternative rock. It showcases the era’s trend of assembling soundtracks with established hits and newly recorded covers, appealing to a broad audience. While the album itself did not achieve major commercial success as a whole, several tracks—especially “Soul to Squeeze”—garnered significant attention and airplay, cementing their place in the decade’s rock canon. The soundtrack remains a cult favorite among fans of the film and collectors of 1990s movie music.
